edits.text: After you have located the source-of-truth data and identified each required deliverable, execute every required write action (each sheet row that needs updating, each invoice that needs creating, each email that needs sending) before declaring the task done. Do not stop after a single representative write or after partial completion — each distinct required deliverable needs its own successful write call. Excessive searching or re-verification between writes causes total task failure when deliverables are left unexecuted.
edits.why: Multiple recent tasks (finance:4014, hr:5125, hr:5035) scored 0.0 because after extensive research the agent never executed the required sheet updates, invoice creations, or follow-up emails — it stopped before doing the writes. This is the dominant action_missed pattern.

edits.text: When source data contains specific values (amounts, names of entities, links, record IDs, totals formatted with thousands separators) that the task or downstream checks require in an output, embed them EXACTLY as they appear in the source — do not round, paraphrase, compute a different number, abbreviate, or omit. Required values (e.g., exact invoice totals in message bodies, employee names in notifications, recording/policy links in follow-up emails) must appear verbatim or the output check fails.
edits.why: wrong_content is the most frequent miss (38 across recent runs). Examples: invoice body missing the required total formatted with comma separators, follow-up emails missing the recording link, notification emails missing the verbatim employee names, computed totals substituting for verbatim source totals.

edits.text: If an action is held by a policy/procedure gate, treat the gate message as a directive to immediately read the requested policy/guideline emails and then proceed with the originally planned writes. Do not interpret being held as a signal to stop or declare done. After reading the requested materials, resume and execute every queued write (each email send, each sheet update, each message) so the held-then-read flow ends in fully completed deliverables, not an abandoned task. Each distinct required deliverable still needs its own successful write call after the gate is satisfied.
edits.why: In hr:5113 the agent was held by a gate asking it to read policy emails, then stopped entirely without resuming — losing every required employee notification and sheet update. Similar early-termination appears in finance:4060 (only a draft created, no sends) and hr:5112 (only searches, no writes). A hold is a continuation prompt, not a stop signal.

edits.text: When a task names multiple specific recipients or message targets (e.g. 'notify each manager', 'email every vendor missing W-9 info', 'alert all employees within X days of the cap', 'send to all listed promotions'), first enumerate the COMPLETE recipient list from the source data, then send one message per recipient. Do not declare the task complete after a single representative send, after a draft, or after only the first batch — every required recipient needs its own successful send call before the task is done.
edits.why: finance:4060 failed to send to tax@ and several vendors; hr:5012 sent to one over-cap employee who should not have received an alert (rule_broken); hr:5112 produced no announcement at all. The agent consistently undercounts the number of independent recipients a multi-recipient task requires.
